title: Six Days Out
subtitle: MES Ransomware, Materiality & Disclosure

brief.userPrompt: Thursday, March 25, 2027, Central Time, six days before quarter end. At 13:40 the Dubuque plant reports a hung manufacturing execution system; at 14:05 the SOC (Security Operations Center) finds ransomware encrypting file servers and the MES at the Rockford data center; at 14:25 CISO Anil Deshmukh isolates the network; at 14:50 CEO Thomas Aldridge declares Level 3 and the CMT convenes at 15:00 with the bridge at (815) 555-0121. The ransom note demands 18 million dollars in cryptocurrency within 72 hours and says 1.2 TB of stolen data will be published. The plants run controllers in manual mode but lot tracking is down at all three plants, the Joliet warehouse system is offline and shipping stops at 15:30, and the ERP integration is locked. The recovery tracker (Business Continuity Manager Ravi Menon) compares recovery with the RTOs at the 4, 8, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hour checkpoints: plant control networks 4 h, MES 8 h, ERP 12 h, shipping 24 h, payroll 48 h; the forensic firm Blackwater Cyber says the last clean MES backup is 31 hours old (the RPO is 15 minutes) and the Dubuque replica is partly encrypted. Pressure points: the Audit Committee Chair Dr. Samuel Obuya must be told within hours and the board within 24 hours; the Disclosure Committee led by General Counsel Marguerite Daley meets by 19:00 and must record a materiality determination (material, not material or not yet determined, with factors, facts known, who decided and the basis) against a planning threshold of 60 million dollars of impact and a day of lost production worth about 8.5 million dollars of sales; CFO Priya Raghavan must give an impact estimate; the ransom decision requires sanctions screening (the group's name partly matches a sanctioned affiliate), the insurer Blue Heron Mutual's consent, notice to the FBI and the consultation of the Audit Committee Chair, and the company policy is not to pay; at 22:10 the attackers post a sample that includes engineering drawings of a drive component for a defense contractor and 3,100 employee records, which raises Department of Defense and state attorney general notices; Fieldmark Equipment's 72-hour supply notice and a penalty after 5 days; payroll must be filed with Northbridge Payroll by 10:00 on Friday; the trading window must close; a local reporter from the Rock River Gazette calls at 18:30 and the story breaks at 20:40; the Form 8-K choice (Item 1.05, Item 8.01 or no filing yet) and its timing with the four business day rule; the board meeting by video at 07:00 on Friday; and employee, dealer and press messages that must match the filing. The SimCell plays the COO, the Chief Communications Officer, Investor Relations, the CIO, the insurer and broker, outside counsel, the forensic negotiator, the FBI Chicago field office, Fieldmark Equipment and Granite Peak Machinery, the external auditor, the agent bank, the plants, reporters, analysts and the attackers.
constraints: Every Ironcrest email address uses the exercise domain ironcrestmachinery.example; customers, vendors, advisers and outlets use fictional .example domains; never a real company, auditor, bank, outlet or person.

SEC filings follow the real Form 8-K format (Item 1.05 content, Item 8.01 without a claim of materiality), are marked as exercise products and carry no real EDGAR accession numbers; all material is an exercise aid and not legal advice; times are Central Time with Eastern Time stated for EDGAR.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; the COO, the Chief Communications Officer, Investor Relations, advisers, regulators, customers, the press and the attackers are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Recovery measured against the RTOs, not against hope; a timely, documented materiality determination; a ransom decision made under policy, sanctions and insurer rules; and one set of facts for the board, the filing, customers, employees and the press.
overview.threat: On Thursday, March 25, 2027 (Central Time), six days before quarter end, the Dubuque plant reported a hung manufacturing execution system at 13:40. At 14:05 the SOC found ransomware encrypting the file servers and the MES at the Rockford data center. CISO Anil Deshmukh isolated the network at 14:25, and the CEO, Thomas Aldridge, declared Level 3 at 14:50, all before STARTEX. The attackers demand 18 million dollars in cryptocurrency within 72 hours and threaten to publish 1.2 TB of stolen data. Their group name partly matches a sanctioned affiliate. Lot tracking is down at all three plants, the Joliet warehouse system is offline and the ERP integration is locked. The forensic firm Blackwater Cyber reports that the last clean MES backup is 31 hours old and that the Dubuque replica is partly encrypted.
overview.operationalImpact:
The CMT convenes at 15:00 on the bridge at (815) 555-0121.

**Operations:** Plants 1 to 3 in Rockford, Beloit and Dubuque run controllers in manual mode. They have no work orders and no lot tracking. Shipping and parts distribution at Joliet stop at 15:30, and the dealer portal cannot show order status.

**Recovery:** Business Continuity Manager Ravi Menon's tracker shows the MES heading past its 8-hour RTO. Recovery must start from a backup 31 hours old against a 15-minute RPO, and nothing can be restored until the forensic firm clears the backups. Each day of lost production is worth about 8.5 million dollars of sales, and CFO Priya Raghavan must give an impact estimate against the 60-million-dollar planning threshold.

**Board and disclosure:** General Counsel Marguerite Daley must tell the Audit Committee Chair, Dr. Samuel Obuya, within hours. The Disclosure Committee meets by 19:00 and must record a materiality determination (material, not material or not yet determined), the Form 8-K choice (Item 1.05, Item 8.01 or no filing yet) and the trading-window closure. The board meets by video at 07:00 on Friday.

**Ransom:** The ransom decision requires sanctions screening, the consent of the insurer Blue Heron Mutual, notice to the FBI and consultation with the Audit Committee Chair. Company policy is not to pay.

**Who is calling:**
- Fieldmark Equipment and Granite Peak Machinery want supply status, which triggers the 72-hour supply notice.
- Northbridge Payroll needs the payroll file by 10:00 Friday.
- The agent bank, the external auditor and analysts are calling.
- A Rock River Gazette reporter calls at 18:30, and the story breaks at 20:40.
- At 22:10 the attackers post a sample that includes engineering drawings of a drive component made for a defense contractor and 3,100 employee records. This raises Department of Defense and state attorney general notices and puts employees on edge.

**Timing:** The story runs from 15:00 Thursday to Friday morning; the time-jump cards compress it into the four hours of exercise time.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to reach and record a timely materiality determination at the 19:00 Disclosure Committee (material, not material or not yet determined), with the Form 8-K choice between Item 1.05, Item 8.01 or no filing yet and the trading-window closure, each stating who decided, when, what was known and the basis.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to handle the 18-million-dollar ransom demand under the IBODAI 3 delegation of authority, completing sanctions screening of the partly matching affiliate, Blue Heron Mutual consent, FBI notice, Audit Committee Chair consultation and the board approval needed above 5 million dollars, while company policy is not to pay.

objectives.name: Recovery Management
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to judge MES, Joliet warehouse and ERP recovery against the IBIARO 3 RTOs and the 4, 8, 12, 24, 48 and 72-hour checkpoints, using the 31-hour-old backup and forensic clearance, and to set a recovery order that protects payroll funding and largest-customer supply before the 5-day finished-goods buffer runs out.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to keep a single fact sheet consistent across the 07:00 Friday board briefing, the 8-K draft, the Fieldmark and Granite Peak supply notices, the employee message after the 3,100-record leak and the Rock River Gazette response.

roles.name: Chief Executive Officer (Chair, Crisis Management Team)
roles.description: Owns the Level 3 crisis: leads the CMT, approves or refuses the ransom, approves public statements, regulator contact and the 8-K with the General Counsel, and keeps the Chair of the Board informed.
standingOrders: Policy Holds: company policy is not to pay; any move away from it needs sanctions screening, insurer consent, FBI notice, Audit Committee Chair consultation and, above 5 million dollars, board approval.
Truth Over Reassurance: tell the board, customers and employees what is known and what is not, even when the news is bad.
Decide on the Record: every crisis decision is logged with the time, what was known and the basis, and no meeting is pushed back to buy time.
Recovery Order: invoke the continuity plan on the BCM's recommendation, not on a vendor's or a plant's promise.

roles.name: Chief Financial Officer
roles.description: Owns the financial impact estimate against the 60-million-dollar planning threshold, along with liquidity, agent bank contact, the insurance claim with Blue Heron Mutual and certification of related filings.
standingOrders: Numbers First: give the Disclosure Committee a dated impact range of about 8.5 million dollars of sales per lost day, stating its assumptions, before 19:00.
Qualitative Counts: weigh the stolen data, customer supply and defense-contractor exposure as well as dollars.
One Script: the agent bank, the auditor and analysts hear only facts that match the fact sheet and the filing.
Protect Cash: keep treasury and payroll funding running for Northbridge Payroll's 10:00 Friday deadline.

roles.name: General Counsel and Corporate Secretary (Disclosure Committee Chair)
roles.description: Manages privilege, outside counsel and Blackwater Cyber, the Disclosure Committee and the 8-K draft, the legal hold, and contact with the FBI, regulators, the Department of Defense and state attorneys general.
standingOrders: Clock Running: the materiality determination follows discovery without unreasonable delay, and an Attorney General delay request does not stop the four business days until it is granted.
Privilege: direct the forensic work through counsel and keep conclusions about fault out of chat and email.
Notify the Chair: send the Audit Committee Chair a written portal note plus a phone call, and use courier and phone if the portal is down.
Sole Channel: only the General Counsel contacts the FBI, the SEC or regulators, telling the CEO first where time allows.

roles.name: Chief Information Security Officer
roles.description: Owns the technical facts on scope and impact, containment of the ransomware, coordination with Blackwater Cyber and restoration of systems once backups are cleared.
standingOrders: Facts, Not Hopes: report what is confirmed, what is suspected and what is unknown, and correct earlier statements promptly.
Containment Before Continuity: restore nothing until the forensic firm clears the backups, whatever the pressure from the plants.
Work Together: share indicators through the General Counsel's FBI channel and with the system vendors, and do not act alone or contact the attackers.
Escalate Fast: tell the General Counsel within one hour of any new exfiltration finding, such as the defense drawings.

roles.name: Business Continuity Manager
roles.description: Owns the BIA and the recovery tracker, records recovery time against each RTO at the 4, 8, 12, 24, 48 and 72-hour checkpoints, and recommends the recovery order.
standingOrders: Measure, Don't Hope: report elapsed time against each RTO and MTPD, and mark a function red when it is red.
Minimum Service: aim first at the minimum acceptable service level in each case: manual lines, 60 percent of Joliet shipments, payroll on cycle.
Recommend Order: propose a recovery order that weighs customer supply, payroll and the quarter close, and leave the decision to the CEO.
Clock the Buffer: track the 5 days of finished goods against the largest customers' inventory of under 10 days.

roles.name: Audit Committee Chair
roles.description: Manages board oversight of the incident disclosure process, the auditor relationship and the consultation on the ransom decision, and reviews whether the disclosure is complete and timely.
standingOrders: Independent Eye: test management's materiality reasoning and the evidence behind it, and do not just accept the conclusion.
Ask the Gaps: make sure each briefing states what is known, what is not known and what the board is being asked to decide.
Oversight, Not Management: advise on the ransom and the disclosure, and leave operational recovery to management.
Minutes Matter: make sure the minutes record what was reported, what directors asked and what was decided.

phases.title: First Hour Fog
phases.goal: Tests whether the CMT turns a declared Level 3 into a disciplined fact base early. It must start the reporting clocks under IDCCI 2 and IBODAI 5 and resist treating materiality as a question for later.
beats: (15:00) CMT convenes on the bridge at (815) 555-0121. CISO Anil Deshmukh's first technical brief is incomplete: MES and Rockford file servers are encrypted, and the scope at Beloit and the ERP integration is 'still being assessed'. Ravi Menon opens the recovery tracker with the MES clock started at 14:05 against its 8-hour IBIARO 3 RTO.
(15:20) Noise item: the SOC flags a failed-login spike on the cloud email suite. The CISO must triage it down as unrelated password-spray noise before more resources go to it.

(15:30) The Joliet Parts Distribution Center stops shipping (normally 4,100 orders a day) and the dealer portal goes blank. SimCell COO reports Plants 1–3 running controllers in manual mode with no work orders or lot tracking.

(15:40) Blackwater Cyber note: the last clean MES backup is 31 hours old against a 15-minute RPO, the Dubuque replica is partly encrypted, and nothing is cleared for restore. The GC must confirm the one-hour CISO-to-GC trigger under IDCCI 2 has been met and schedule the Disclosure Committee within four hours.

(15:50) Deputy GC asks who has called the Blue Heron Mutual claims line. IBODAI 5 requires notice within 24 hours and prior consent before Blackwater Cyber and Harrow Fenn LLP are formally retained, and the CFO has not yet called.

phases.title: The Determination
phases.goal: Tests whether the Disclosure Committee reaches and records a timely materiality determination, makes the Form 8-K choice and closes the trading window under IDCCI 4 and 5 while outside parties press for answers. This phase advances the narrative clock to about 18:30–19:30.
beats: Time jump (18:30): the MES has passed its 4-hour checkpoint and will miss the 8-hour checkpoint at 22:05. CFO Priya Raghavan must give an impact estimate: about 8.5 million dollars of sales per day of lost production at all plants, compared with the 60-million-dollar planning threshold and the 5-day finished-goods buffer.

(18:30) A Rock River Gazette reporter calls the Chief Communications Officer (SimCell) with a 20:00 deadline. He says a source told him 'all three plants are shut down and customer data was stolen', which is inaccurate. The CEO must approve a holding statement drawn from the fact sheet.

(18:45) Fieldmark Equipment and Granite Peak Machinery demand supply status, which starts the 72-hour supply notice. The agent bank and the external auditor also call for a briefing. These calls split CFO and GC attention just before the committee meets.

(19:00) The Disclosure Committee meets. The GC as chair must record the IDCCI 4 decision: material, not material or not yet determined, with factors, known facts, who decided with CEO and CFO concurrence, and the basis. It also records the 8-K choice (Item 1.05, Item 8.01 or no filing yet) with the four-business-day clock and the trading-window closure.
(19:20) GC briefs Audit Committee Chair Dr. Samuel Obuya, who asks whether the record will hold up if the facts change overnight.

phases.title: Pay or Refuse
phases.goal: Tests the single high-consequence ransom decision under the IBODAI 3 delegation of authority and the no-pay policy, made with the story already public and the stolen data starting to leak. This phase advances the narrative clock to about 20:40–22:30.
beats: (20:40) The Rock River Gazette story breaks. A fictional wire bulletin follows, analysts email Investor Relations, and the social listening report shows a 'plant shutdown, layoffs coming' narrative spreading among employees.

(21:00) Blackwater Cyber gives the smoking gun: an unauthorized domain-admin session through a vendor remote-access account, a staging script on the Rockford file server, and outbound transfers that match the 1.2 TB claim. Sanctions screening returns a partial match between the group's name and a sanctioned affiliate.

(21:30) DECISION POINT: pay the 18-million-dollar ransom for a decryptor, or refuse and rebuild from the 31-hour-old backup. Paying could restore the MES before the 5-day buffer runs out but carries sanctions exposure, needs Blue Heron Mutual consent, FBI notice, consultation with Dr. Samuel Obuya and board approval above 5 million dollars, and goes against policy. Refusing means a longer outage and certain publication of the data. The CEO must record who decided, when and on what basis.

(22:10) The attackers post a sample: engineering drawings of a drive component made for a defense contractor and 3,100 employee records. The GC must decide on Department of Defense and state attorney general notices and whether this changes the 19:00 determination. The CHRO's employee message must match the fact sheet.
(22:20) A reporter asks for comment on the leak with a deadline of 22:45. Every quote must agree with the board pre-read and the 8-K draft.

phases.title: Restore and Verify
phases.goal: Tests whether the CMT judges recovery claims against IBIARO 3 RTOs and checkpoints rather than hope, and briefs the board with the same facts used in the filing and stakeholder notices. This phase advances the narrative clock to Friday 06:00–10:00.
beats: (06:30 Friday) The CIO (SimCell) reports the MES 'back up' from the 31-hour-old backup. Ravi Menon's tracker shows lot reconciliation for 31 hours of production is still outstanding and the MES is past its 12-hour checkpoint and nearing its 24-hour MTPD. Fieldmark Equipment demands a written guarantee that its lots are traceable.

(07:00) The board meets by video, with Board Chair Eleanor Whitcomb, Dr. Samuel Obuya and Karen Lindqvist. They ask: how do we know the restore is clean, and has Blackwater Cyber cleared the backup? The briefing must match the 8-K draft, supply notices and employee message.

(08:15) Technical hurdle: the restored ERP integration reintroduces the vendor remote-access account, and the warehouse software vendor needs a ticket and signed access request before Joliet can restart. This delays progress toward 60 percent of normal parts orders.

(09:00) Northbridge Payroll needs the payroll file by 10:00. With the HR integration unverified, the CFO and CHRO must choose between running the prior cycle's file and making manual adjustments, while treasury confirms payroll funding.

(09:45) Tedious reconciliation: the GC confirms whether the Item 1.05 or 8.01 decision stands and when an 8-K/A or re-determination is due before the 5:30 p.m. Eastern EDGAR cut-off. The BCM logs actual recovery times against each RTO. ENDEX.

All three plants were on normal three-shift production for the quarter-end push, and Joliet was on track for its usual 4,100 parts orders. Life-safety, fire and gas systems at every site report normal; they run on separate networks. Here is what has happened so far today. At 13:40 Plant 3 Dubuque reported a hung MES. objectiveCapabilities.why: The Disclosure Committee has to turn the CISO's confirmed, suspected and unknown facts and the CFO's impact range into a materiality determination at 19:00. It then has to choose the 8-K item and revisit the record as the Beloit, exfiltration and leak facts change.

The determination and the 8-K approval belong to named holders under the delegation of authority: the General Counsel and the CEO, with the CFO concurring. Legal, finance and security have to work in one process from one set of facts.

The 18-million-dollar demand tests the ICMP 6 and IBODAI 3 chain: sanctions screening through outside counsel, Blue Heron Mutual consent, FBI and CISA notice, the forensic firm's view, Audit Committee Chair consultation and board approval above 5 million dollars, all against a no-pay policy.

Players have to restore the MES, Joliet warehouse system, ERP and payroll in the IBIARO 4 recovery order. They work from the 31-hour-old backup only after forensic clearance, rebuild rather than clean, and track each system against its IBIARO 3 RTO and checkpoints.
The board briefing, 8-K draft, customer supply notices, employee message, analyst answers and press response all have to pass the IDCCI 6 consistency check and use only figures from the fact sheet.

hotwash.methodDescription: Ask the room for three things that went well and three that broke or failed, so you get strengths and gaps before memories fade. Go around the room team by team (CMT, IT/Security, Legal/Disclosure, Communications, Operations), write every item on the whiteboard in two columns, and don't debate an item until each team has had its turn.

questions.text: At the 19:00 Disclosure Committee you had I-09 from five minutes earlier: exfiltration confirmed, contents unknown. At 21:00, I-13 confirmed about 1.2 TB taken, including a Finance close share, six days before quarter end. What did you record at 19:00: material, not material or not yet determined? Did you choose Item 1.05, Item 8.01 or no filing yet, and did you close the trading window? Who decided, and on what basis? When I-13 changed the facts, did anyone reopen that determination, or did the 19:00 decision stand by default?

When the I-14 Ransom Decision Paper landed at 21:30, the sanctions screen was unresolved (an 82% match to MOLTEN SYNDICATE, and a wallet one hop from a designated cluster). Blue Heron Mutual said it could not consent, and the FBI recommended against paying. Did you work through the IBODAI 3 delegation of authority step by step: sanctions, insurer, FBI notice, the Audit Committee Chair and the board approval needed above 5 million dollars? Or did the 15% discount and the 24-hour clock pull you into a debate about paying? When did you first contact the FBI and the insurer, and what would have let you close this decision faster?

I-13 showed that the attacker came in through svc_wmsvendor, the Joliet warehouse vendor's own support account, with an MFA bypass on 22 March. Up to then, when did you stop trusting vendor remote access, the Dubuque replica and the 31-hour-old backup? When did you call the vendor, and did you disable all vendor accounts and reset krbtgt twice before you planned any rebuild? Or did the recovery plan assume the environment was clean?

The BCM tracker in I-14 put a refuse-and-rebuild MES at minimum service around day 4 to 5, plus manual re-entry of 31 hours of lots. Against the 5-day finished-goods buffer and Fieldmark's penalty clause, did you judge MES, Joliet and ERP against the IBIARO 3 RTOs at the 4, 8, 12 and 24-hour checkpoints, or against hope? What recovery order did you set to protect payroll funding and the largest customers? Did operations understand what the technical team meant by 'rebuilt, not cleaned' and 'forensic clearance', and did the technical team understand what operations meant?

At 18:32 the Rock River Gazette (I-07) claimed that all three plants were shut down and customer data was stolen, with a 20:00 deadline. What did you tell the reporter before you knew the facts, and did you approve the words 'cybersecurity incident' or 'ransomware'? After I-09 and I-13 confirmed HR data was stolen, did that holding statement still match the employee message, the Fieldmark and Granite Peak supply notices, the 8-K draft and the 07:00 Friday board briefing? Who owned the single fact sheet, and where did the versions drift apart?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Special agent, cyber squad, FBI Chicago field office
simcellScripts.trigger: The General Counsel (or the CEO on the GC's instruction under IBODAI 3) calls to report the ransomware and extortion demand, or says they will give the FBI notice before any ransom decision (I-14).
hardQuestions: "Thanks for calling. What's your case contact, and is outside counsel on the line? Do you have the ransom note, both wallet addresses and the negotiator's chat log preserved? Send me the indicators, not a summary."
"Are the gateway logs from ICM-RA-01 and the file-server images under a legal hold, or is your team still rebuilding over them? If they're gone, I can't help you attribute anything."

"Those drawings say CUI and export-controlled. Has your defense customer been told, and have you checked whether your contract requires you to report to the Department of Defense? That clock isn't mine, but somebody will ask."

"If you're thinking of asking DOJ to delay your disclosure, understand that it's a formal request and it isn't my call. Do you have a reason that is actually national security or public safety, or do you just want more time?"
concessions: Once wallet addresses, indicators and preserved logs are sent: confirms the FBI recommends against payment, gives the CEO a line the decision record can cite ("FBI notified at [time]; FBI recommends against payment; decision is the company's"), and says whether the wallets are known to it.
Once the company gives a written timeline and a single point of contact: agrees to share any decryptor or indicators it has from other victims of this actor, through counsel.
Will not clear the sanctions question and will not tell the company to pay or not pay.

hardQuestions: "Happy to help. What's your P1 ticket number? It'll start WSV-. No ticket, no engineer. That's in our support agreement."
"I need a signed Remote Access Request on your letterhead from an officer, naming the engineer and the change window. Who's signing it?"

"You're saying our support account was the way in? Our records show no technician worked on March 22. Before you put that in writing anywhere, it needs to go to our legal team. Who on your side is your counsel?"
"The earliest window for our engineer is 13:00 Central, and it's a 4-hour change. Do you want the account set up with MFA on your side? Legacy protocol access was your configuration, not ours."
concessions: With a P1 ticket raised and a signed Remote Access Request from an officer: creates a new named-user account (no shared service account) with MFA enforced, and offers to move the engineer up to 11:00 CT.
With a written request through counsel: exports its own access logs for the svc_wmsvendor account for March 20 to 26 and preserves them for the forensic firm.
Will not accept liability on the phone or agree that its account was the root cause.

"What is your business-interruption estimate per day, and when did the 8-hour waiting period start? I need a number with a date on it, not 'not yet determined'."

Will reconsider consent to a payment only after a written sanctions clearance from counsel and confirmation of law-enforcement notice. Never before.

simcellScripts.trigger: The 18:32 phone slip (I-07) or the 22:20 phone slip (I-15b), or the Chief Communications Officer calls the reporter back with or without an approved statement.
hardQuestions: "My source says all three plants are shut down and customer data was stolen. Is that wrong? Then tell me what's right, on the record. My deadline is 20:00 for the web edition."
"Is it ransomware? Yes or no. 'Cybersecurity incident' tells my readers nothing."
"The hackers just posted what look like employee Social Security records and defense drawings. Did you pay, or are you going to? Is this material for your shareholders? I have until 22:45."
"If I don't hear back, the story says Ironcrest declined to comment. Who's your spokesperson, and can I quote them by name?"
concessions: If an approved holding statement arrives before the deadline: quotes it and includes "the plants continue to operate in manual mode" alongside the source's claim.
If the company gives specific facts on the record that contradict the source (no customer data confirmed so far): runs a write-through with the correction and the attribution.
Will hold for 15 more minutes, once only, if the CCO gives a time-certain promise of a statement.

simcellScripts.trigger: Players return Fieldmark's calls (I-03, I-08), send or draft the supply notice, or respond to the Friday request for a written lot-traceability guarantee (I-17).
hardQuestions: "Our planners see nothing from your portal and nobody at Joliet answers. The contract needs written notice of any supply disruption within 72 hours. When do I get it, and does it give dates or just 'temporary IT disruption'?"
"Are you invoking force majeure? Because if you are, I want it in writing tonight, and my lawyers will read it next to whatever you file with the SEC."
"I need a signed guarantee before 12:00 that every drive you've shipped to us since March 24 is traceable to its heats and test records. Your MES was down. How can you sign that?"
"Your newspaper says your data is out. Were any of our drawings or orders in it?"
concessions: Once there is a written supply status with dates that match the company's other statements: accepts it as the 72-hour notice and agrees to talk again in 24 hours.
Instead of a blanket guarantee, will accept a written lot-reconciliation plan with manual-mode production records for the affected period, and will hold off quarantining stock while it is checked.
Will not waive the 5-day penalty clause, but will agree in writing on when the clock started.

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. Discussion explores decisions and gaps in Ironcrest's plans, not the performance of individuals.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players accept the facts in each module and inject as written, even where they would want more information.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures: the Crisis Management Plan, the Corporate Delegation of Authority, the BIA and recovery order and the disclosure procedures. Where a plan is silent, players say so and state what they would decide.
Players know only what the modules and injects have told them up to that point. Facts that later injects discover are not available to players earlier.

Materials marked as an exercise aid are not legal advice. Disclosure deadlines, sanctions questions and insurer terms are discussed for learning, and in a real event players would check the current rule and their counsel.
Players speak for their own seat on the Crisis Management Team and decide within the authority that seat holds.
artificialities: Time is compressed. Each module jumps the narrative clock forward (to 18:30 Thursday, 20:40 Thursday and 06:30 Friday), and events between modules are summarised on facilitator time-jump cards.

A Simulation Cell (SimCell) plays everyone outside the room: the COO, the CIO, the CHRO and CCO offices, Blackwater Cyber, Harrow Fenn LLP, Blue Heron Mutual, the FBI Chicago field office, the Joliet warehouse software vendor, Northbridge Payroll, customers, the agent bank, the external auditor, board members not present, analysts, reporters and the attackers.
Systems such as the MES, ERP, the Joliet warehouse system, the SIEM, the board portal and the bank portals are named as they appear in the plans. They are not touched or changed during play.
Injects arrive on paper or on screen as emails, phone slips, alerts and leak-site captures. Players respond by discussing them and do not send any real messages, filings or notices.
Exercise documents such as the materiality worksheet, the ransom decision paper and the recovery tracker are simplified for discussion. They are not complete legal or technical records.

**Module 1: First Hour Fog (Thursday, March 25, 2027, 15:00–16:00 CT)**

It is 15:00 Central Time on Thursday, March 25, 2027, six days before quarter end. All three plants were on normal three-shift production for the quarter-end push, and Joliet was on track for its usual 4,100 parts orders. Life-safety, fire and gas systems at every site report normal; they run on separate networks.

At 13:40 Plant 3 Dubuque reported a hung MES. At 14:05 the SOC found ransomware encrypting the file servers and the MES at the Rockford data center. At 14:25 CISO Anil Deshmukh isolated the network, and at 14:50 the CEO declared Level 3. The Crisis Management Team is now joining the bridge. Beyond Rockford, nobody yet knows which systems are affected, what data is involved or how long recovery will take.

**Module 2: The Determination (Thursday, March 25, 18:30–19:30 CT)**

It is 18:30 Central Time. Three and a half hours have passed since the CMT first met. The MES encryption at Rockford is confirmed, and the ransom note demands 18 million dollars within 72 hours and threatens to publish 1.2 TB of data. Blackwater Cyber reports that the last clean MES backup is the Wednesday 07:05 snapshot, 31 hours before encryption. The Dubuque replica is partly encrypted, and no backup will be cleared until a 12- to 18-hour persistence sweep is finished. About 940 GB of outbound traffic on Tuesday night is under review. The Blue Heron Mutual notice and vendor-consent questions have been raised.

Ravi Menon's tracker shows the MES passed its 4-hour checkpoint at 18:05 with no recovery under way. It is RED and will miss its 8-hour RTO at 22:05. The plants are still running controllers in manual mode with no work orders or lot tracking. Joliet has shipped nothing since 15:30, the ERP integration is still locked, and Fieldmark is calling. Working figures: a full lost day at all plants is about 8.5 million dollars of sales, and the planning threshold is 60 million dollars of expected pre-tax impact. The Disclosure Committee meets at 19:00.

**Module 3: Pay or Refuse (Thursday, March 25, 20:40–22:30 CT)**

It is 20:40 Central Time (21:40 Eastern). Since the 19:00 Disclosure Committee, Blackwater Cyber has confirmed encryption at Plant 2 Beloit as well as Rockford, and has tied part of Tuesday night's outbound traffic to the Engineering and HR shares. Exfiltration is CONFIRMED, but what was taken is still UNKNOWN. The board portal is still down because single sign-on is isolated. At 20:40 the Rock River Gazette published its story online: 'Ironcrest hit by cyberattack; plants scramble, data reportedly stolen.'

The MES will miss its 8-hour RTO at 22:05, and no backup is cleared. Joliet has shipped no parts orders for 5 hours 10 minutes, and its 24-hour RTO runs out at 15:30 Friday. The plants are still in manual mode with no lot tracking, so each is using up its 5-day finished-goods buffer.
